name: topopen_addloop
description: Topology Pen Add-Loop: frozen reference behaviour of the loop walk and of the single cut fraction. Given an input mesh, a SEED EDGE and one scalar fraction on that seed edge, the tool walks a ring of edges and inserts exactly one new vertex on each edge of that ring, at the SAME scalar (per-edge orientation may flip it to 1-t), splitting each crossed face. A case asserts three independent things: the exact SET of crossed edges, the fraction on each, and the resulting geometry.
why_not_keyed_on_a_click: The mapping from a pointer position to the scalar is a targeting question, and the capture rig's own aim was measured to deliver the press at the highlighted element's screen centroid rather than at the intended point on it -- so a click-keyed fixture would freeze the rig's aim, not the engine's law. The scalar is therefore an INPUT here, read back from the reference run.
set_is_asserted_explicitly: expected.not_crossed_edges lists every input edge that must receive no new vertex. A fixture that only pins positions for an assumed moved set cannot detect a wrong set; this one can.
source: Captured from a reference polygon modeller through the atlas gesture harness (wave-1 corpus, 2026-07-26); the post-gesture meshes are the reference's own dumps to full float precision. The scalar and the crossed-edge set are derived from those dumps by locating each new vertex on the input mesh's edges (closest point on segment); the maximum residual off an input edge is reported per case.

provenance.harness: private atlas gesture harness (wave-1 corpus, long-lived --serve session)
provenance.notes: Keyed on (mesh, seed edge, scalar), never on a click pixel: the rig's aim was measured delivering the press at the highlighted element's screen centroid, so a click-keyed fixture would freeze the aim, not the law. 5 of 8 cases are open spans (dV=N+1, dE=2N+1, dF=N); 3 are closed rings (N, 2N, N).

parameters.notes: drive record read from tests/fixtures/topopen_addloop.json:110; Every cell carries its own `input.scalar` (lines 110, 408, 674, 1063, 1677, 2377, 3585, 5805) — one cut fraction per case, the tool's single parameter. `input.seed_edge` is the seed and stays out as stand, and `input.scalar_orientation` is a prose statement of the measurement convention, not a value. These scalars are the RECOVERED equivalent of the capture's press position: the fixture's own `why_not_keyed_on_a_click` says the pointer-to-scalar mapping was deliberately NOT frozen because the rig's aim was measured landing at the highlighted element's screen centroid. Recorded under the fixture's own key `scalar` rather than the public `mesh.addLoop` parameter `position` (source/commands/mesh/loop_slice.d:116,144) on purpose: the conformance test converts one to the other with a per-face orientation flip (t = flip ? 1 - scalar : scalar, tests/test_topopen_addloop_conformance.d:145-147), so per cell they are not the same number and equating them would be a claim, not a transcription.
